Decision framework

Not the most ZIP codes. The best operating combination.

The recommendation is designed to compound value as territories are added. The four-territory package captures the essential northwest Chicago employment engines; six broadens the northern platform; eight adds Oak Brook and Naperville/Bolingbrook; ten creates a substantial north/northwest/western Chicago regional network.

4
THE CORE

4-Territory Opportunity

Maximum impact with the fewest territories. Anchors John’s home market and immediately captures Schaumburg, O’Hare/Elk Grove and the north-suburban institutional corridor.

Best balance of home-market control + corporate + DOT/logistics + institutional demand.

THE GROWTH PLATFORM

More healthcare, government, schools, dense workforce and Chicago-edge access.

How the AI ranked the combinations

Market fit over raw population.

Inputs used

  • Official territory-to-ZIP assignments from the uploaded U.S. Territory ZIP Code Report.
  • User-supplied FranTerra/GBBIS maps showing territory geometry and business-location overlays.
  • FranTerra demographic report/screenshot information previously supplied for selected territories.
  • Public information from municipalities, economic-development agencies, airport authorities, the U.S. Navy and employer/public-sector sources.

AI evaluation factors

  • Contiguity and practical mobile-service coverage.
  • Transportation, DOT, cargo, warehousing and industrial concentration.
  • Government, police/fire/public works and other public-sector opportunity.
  • Healthcare, education, utilities and large institutional employers.
  • Corporate headquarters, regional offices and large employment centers.
  • Diversification: avoiding a portfolio that depends on one customer type.
